topics.topic: Legacy room-name correction procedure, verification, and failure gating before migration
questions: What concrete legacy action corrects a room name, how does the owner verify that every selected project's rooms were corrected successfully, and what stops export or import when a required correction cannot be made?
What exact legacy action or procedure changes a room name, including for an archived project, and what observable result proves that every selected room now satisfies the naming rule before export?

What happens when a violating room name cannot be corrected or the owner cannot verify the correction: is the whole export stopped, is that project excluded, or may the import proceed despite the violation?

quotes:
So the owner, before making the export on the VPS (R0-72), corrects
there every room name of the projects to be picked that breaks this rule
(owner, 2026-11-23, State 0 round-59 T1). That correction is made in the
legacy v1 instance, by its own means, before the export; the legacy instances
stand outside this document's guarantees (Actors).

The
import then copies names the owner has already checked; it writes no name of
its own and refuses none.

The owner makes the export of a source with a one-time migration script run on
that source's host. The script is not a Registry operation: production Registry
gains no export action, and the source keeps none after the migration.
judgement.why: State 0 fixes successful legacy correction and owner checking as prerequisites before export while explicitly placing the legacy instance outside Registry's guarantees, so the concrete legacy procedure, verification evidence, and operational response to failure belong to State 7 notes.
